text:
alex_lewis: Heads up — enterprise customer (eu-prod) reporting elevated latency and 401s. They say traffic from DE/FR is routing to us-west and getting ~200ms. Also noticed unexpected spike in billed tokens during the same window.

maria_k: Ack. Which API endpoint are they hitting? region pinned in request?

alex_lewis: /v1/chat/completions, no explicit region header. Using standard api.redwood.ai host. Example client IPs they provided: 78.14.23.45, 185.22.11.7.

ingrid_ops: Can you paste one of the failing request IDs and a sample curl we can repro with?

alex_lewis: request id: req_0a9f3c. Repro curl they used:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-rl","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

Returns a 200-ish latency when hitting eu, but this customer gets 503/401 and then retries which ends up hitting us-west.

support_bot: Incident created INC-2026-3143 (geoip-mismatch). Labels: dns, routing, billing-impact.

tim_oncall: I ran dig from a DE resolver (1.1.1.1) earlier and got api.redwood.ai -> 54.72.11.9 (us-west) with TTL 300. Can you confirm their resolver?

maria_k: Customer traceroute attached: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (54.72.11.9), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
1  local-gw (192.168.1.1)  1.2 ms  1.0 ms  1.1 ms
7  isp-peering (89.27.0.2)  18.2 ms  19.0 ms  18.6 ms
12 us-west-edge (54.72.11.9)  180.2 ms  179.9 ms  180.5 ms
```

ingrid_ops: That looks like a GeoIP DB mismatch at the authoritative layer or their ISP doing geo overrides. dl_dns, can you check our authoritative answers in EU POPs?

dl_dns: Looking. Our authoritative (ns1.redwood.net) currently returns 54.72.11.9 for api.redwood.ai when queried from some European ASNs — seems the GeoIP table flagged those IPs as NA due to a stale ASN->continent mapping. TTLs are 300.

maria_k: Could the fallback policy be kicking in? If an EU edge is unhealthy, requests fallback to next available which might be us-west. But the 401s worry me — token scoping is region-agnostic normally. Any chance they are using a region-scoped token?

alex_lewis: Customer confirmed token is global. They say auth errors happen right away for some requests, others succeed but with high latency. Billing spike: they had 1200 retries from their SDK in 40 minutes — each retry counted.

tim_oncall: Short-term mitigation: reduce DNS TTL to 60 on API hostname and push a corrected GeoIP mapping to authoritative DNS. Also enable sticky routing by sending a 302 to eu subdomain? Not ideal.

ingrid_ops: Steps I propose:
1) Push GeoIP table correction to authoritative (patch mapping for the affected ASN ranges).
2) Reduce TTL to 60 and force re-issue.
3) Add temporary traffic-shepherd rule in our edge to prefer eu-serving for requests with X-Forwarded-For inside EU ranges.
4) Investigate why auth 401s appear — pull app logs for req_0a9f3c and surrounding.

maria_k: For repro: @support -> ask customer to run `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai` and `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai` and paste outputs. Also ask for `curl -I -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" https://<ip>` to see TLS cert and virtual host behavior.

alex_lewis: I'll send that now. Customer dig results: 54.72.11.9 (1.1.1.1) and 18.206.33.12 (8.8.8.8). Mixed answers.

dl_dns: Mixed authoritative answers confirm inconsistent steering. Could be geoip cache at CDN layer also stale; need to purge CDN Geo cache and reload.

tim_oncall: I triggered a GeoIP DB refresh on edge nodes and purged geo caches in eu-pop-2. Will watch metrics.

support_bot: Update: Geoip DB refresh pushed at 2026-03-17T12:34:50Z. Automated rollback if >1% error increase in 10m.

ingrid_ops: Regarding billing, we should credit the customer for retry-induced excessive usage while we diagnose; ops-billing, ping?

maria_k: Billing ops looped in. They suggest crediting failed retry token charges and offering a service credit for SLA breach window.

alex_lewis: Customer confirmed after refresh that dig from DE returns 18.206.33.12 (eu-edge) and traceroute latency dropped to 24ms. No more 401s observed in last 10 minutes.

dl_dns: Root cause: stale GeoIP->ASN mapping in our authoritative DNS steering rules plus CDN geo-cache not refreshed. Fixes: update mapping, reduce TTL temporarily, add monitoring for geo answer drift.

tim_oncall: Follow-ups: implement weekly automated GeoIP DB sync, add alert when >5% queries from EU return NA answers, and add a sticky region header option in SDK to allow bypassing DNS when necessary.

ingrid_ops: I'll create a short postmortem with timeline and customer impact, and note the billing credit.

maria_k: Nice job everyone. alex, please confirm customer OK with closure and credit amount.

alex_lewis: Customer accepted credit and closure. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
